::: {.collapse-item #events-oct2025 title="10/15/2025 -- 2025 Webinar Series: Scott Berry" parent="#events-list"}
Our open access zoom webinar took place on Wednesday, October 15, 2025 from noon - 1pm ET. Questions for the speaker and discussion followed the presentation.

Scott Berry (Berry Consultants, LLC) presented: "Bayesian vs Bayesian Controversies in Clinical Trials".

[Webinar Details](https://github.com/isba-biostatspharma/isba-biostatspharma.github.io/blob/master/docs/October%202025%20Webinar.pdf)\
[Watch the recording on the ISBA YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HlGrtN7JwBI)
:::

::: {.collapse-item #events1 title="06/27/2025 -- BBP2025: Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics Section Conference" parent="#events-list"}
The first ever [Bayesian Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics Section Conference (BBP2025)](https://bnp14.org/bbp2025/) took place on Friday, June 27, 2025 at the University of California Los Angeles (UCLA), USA, following the [Bayesian Nonparametric Section Conference (BNP14)](https://bnp14.org/) held June 23-June 27.

The aim of BBP2025 was to promote the advancement, application, and dissemination of Bayesian methods in the fields of Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics. The conference served as a platform for researchers and practitioners, within these fields, to strengthen communication and collaboration across academic and industrial communities.

The scope of the conference encompassed a wide range of topics, including the many facets of biostatistics, as well as the application of statistics to medicine. This included both clinical and non-clinical aspects of pharmaceutical statistics, such as the optimal design and analysis of clinical trials (drugs, biologics, and medical devices), Bayesian adaptive trial designs, medical decision-making, benefit-risk assessment for regulatory decision-making, model-based drug development (pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, pharmacogenetics), biostatistics, bioinformatics and its applications to genetics, genomics, proteomics, and pharmacoeconomics.
:::

::: {.collapse-item #events2 title="07/19/2024 -- 2024 Webinar Series: Shuangjie Zhang" parent="#events-list"}
Our open access zoom webinar took place on Friday, July 19, 2024 from noon - 1pm CT. Questions for the speaker and discussion followed the presentation.

Shuangjie Zhang (University of California Santa Cruz) presented his paper entitled: "Sparse Bayesian Group Factor Model for Feature Interactions in Multiple Count Tables Data".

[Webinar Details](https://github.com/isba-biostatspharma/isba-biostatspharma.github.io/blob/master/docs/July%202024%20Webinar.pdf)
:::

::: {.collapse-item #events3 title="04/29/2024 -- 2023 Paper Competition Award Winners Webinar" parent="#events-list"}
Our open access zoom webinar took place on April 29, 2024 from 1pm - 3pm CT, featuring the 2023 paper competition award winners. Questions for speakers and discussion followed each presenter.

Noirrit Chandra (University of Texas at Dallas) presented his paper entitled: "Bayesian Nonparametric Common Atoms Regression for Generating Synthetic Controls in Clinical Trials".

Rodney Sparapani (Medical College of Wisconsin) presented his paper entitled: "Nonparametric failure time: Time-to-event machine learning with heteroskedastic Bayesian additive regression trees and low information omnibus Dirichlet process mixtures".

[Webinar Details](2023%20Paper%20Winners%20Webinar%20.docx%20(4).pdf)
:::

::: {.collapse-item #news2025 title="03/30/2026 -- The 2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Paper Award Recipients are announced!" parent="#news-list"}
The BioPharm Section is pleased to present the 2025 Best Paper and Junior Researcher Award recipients along with two Junior Researcher Award recognitions of having highly reviewed papers amongst a competitive pool of submissions in this award category.

The 2025 Best Paper Award Recipient

**Peter Thall** and the paper, ["Precision generalized phase I-II Designs"](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomtc/ujaf043), with co-authors: Saijun Zhao, Ying Yuan, Juhee Lee, Pavlos Msaousel, and Yong Zang.

The 2025 Junior Researcher Award Recipient

**Andrea Sottosanti** and the paper, ["Bayesian Mapping of Mortality Clusters"](https://doi.org/10.1093/biostatistics/kxaf028). Co-authors: Enrico Bovo, Pietro Belloni, and Giovanna Boccuzzo.

2025 Junior Researcher Award recognitions

**Anil Anderson**, "Bayesian Analysis of Clinical Trials with a Delayed Treatment Effect". Co-authors: Ethan M. Alt, Amarjot Kaur, Qing Li, Jia Hua, Tianjian Zhou, and Joseph G. Ibrahim.

**Federica Stolf and Lorenzo Mauri**, ["Pathway-based Bayesian factor models for gene expression data"](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.2601.13419). Co-authors: Amy H. Herring, Cameron Miller, and David B. Dunson.

**Paper Reviewers**: Valerie Poynor, Yuan Ji, Fan Bu, Giorgio Paulon, and Jacob Fiksel.
:::

::: {.collapse-item #news2024 title="08/15/2025 -- The 2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Best Paper Awards Call for Submissions" parent="#news-list"}
The ISBA Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics Section is pleased to call for submissions for the 2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Junior Researcher Award, and the 2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Best Paper Award. The deadline for submissions is ~~November 1, 2025~~ now extended to **November 15, 2025**. Please prepare nominations as a single pdf file following the convention LASTNAME_FIRSTNAME.pdf so the file name corresponds to the nominee and then email them to isba.biostatspharma@gmail.com, provided the file is less than 25MB. For files larger than 25MB, please contact Valerie Poynor at vpoynor@fullerton.edu to make appropriate alternative arrangements. Please note:\
1. A manuscript may only be submitted to one of the two award categories.\
2. Nominees may only be nominated once across both award categories.\
3. Nominee submissions with coauthors do not disqualify the coauthors from being nominated for any award via a different submission.\
For further details about rules and eligibility, please see [Awards Tab](#awards).

**2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Junior Researcher Award**

The ISBA Biostats and Pharma Junior Researcher Award is to be awarded to a student or early career researcher who has made important original contributions to either the foundations, theoretical developments, and/or general methodology of Bayesian analysis in the field of biostatistics or pharmaceutical statistics, or that has solved a substantive applied problem that has potential to impact statistical practice in the biological and pharmaceutical sciences.

**2025 ISBA Biostats and Pharma Best Paper Award**

The ISBA Biostats and Pharma Best Paper Award is bestowed upon an individual or individuals based on their innovative use of Bayesian statistics to solve a high-impact problem in the biostatistical and pharmaceutical sciences.

In odd numbered years, the award is presented for a paper published in a refereed journal that makes important original contributions to the foundations, theoretical developments, and/or general methodology of Bayesian analysis in the biostatistical and pharmaceutical sciences. In even numbered years, the award is presented for a paper published in a refereed journal that presents distinguished work performed by a collaborative team of statisticians and practitioners with regards to an application of Bayesian methods to an applied problem in the biological and pharmaceutical sciences.
:::

      About Section
    ============================-->
    <section id="about">
      <div class="container">
        <div class="row">
          <div class="col-lg-10">
            <h2>Our Mission</h2>
            <p>The mission of the Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics Section of the International Society for Bayesian Analysis is to promote the research, application and dissemination of Bayesian methods and solutions for problems in Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical statistics. This covers the many facets of biostatistics, and statistics applied to medicine comprising both the clinical and non-clinical aspects of pharmaceutical statistics. It includes, non exhaustively, optimal design and analysis of clinical trials (drugs, biologics, and medical devices), Bayesian adaptive trial designs, medical decision making, Benefit: risk assessment for regulatory decision making, model-based drug development (pharmacokinetics / pharmacodynamics / pharmacogenetics), biostatistics, bioinformatics and its applications to genetics, genomics and proteomics, and pharmacoeconomics.</p>
          </div>
        </div>
      </div>
    </section>

    <!--==========================
      Bylaws Section
    ============================-->
    <section id="bylaws" class="section-with-bg">
      <div class="container wow fadeInUp">
        <div class="section-header">
          <h2>The Bylaws</h2>
        </div>
          <ol type="1">
              <li><b>The Name of the Section</b></li>
              <p>ISBA Section on Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical Statistics (ISBA/Biostat&Pharma).</p>
              <li><b>The Purpose of the Section</b></li>
              <p>The primary purpose of the Section is to promote the research, application and dissemination of Bayesian methods and solutions for problems in Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical statistics. This covers the many facets of biostatistics, and statistics applied to medicine comprising both the clinical and non-clinical aspects of pharmaceutical statistics. It includes, non exhaustively, optimal design and analysis of clinical trials (drugs, biologics, and medical devices), Bayesian adaptive trial designs, medical decision making, Benefit: risk assessment for regulatory decision making, model-based drug development (pharmacokinetics / pharmacodynamics / pharmacogenetics), biostatistics, bioinformatics and its applications to genetics, genomics and proteomics, and pharmacoeconomics. In order to achieve this purpose, the section activities consist of:
              <ul>
              <li>Promoting education and use of Bayesian methods in Biostatistics and Pharmaceutical statistics by developing workshops, courses and webinars for students and practitioners</li>
              <li>Organizing short courses, workshops, conferences, webinars and sessions within ISBA meetings</li>
              <li>Promoting interactions among academia, regulatory agencies and industry</li>
              <li>Promoting interactions and outreach to pharma, medical device, and clinical trial professionals, with a focus on exploring how Bayesian statistics can solve their problems and fit their specific needs</li>
              <li>Connecting and bringing visibility to initiatives from academia, regulatory agencies and industry aimed at spreading Bayesian methods and ideas, by federating them under a common brand</li>
              <li>Fostering faster/easier availability of Bayesian methods, via devepment of software packages and publication in field-specific journals</li>
              </ul></p>
              <li><b>The Offices, Duties, and Terms of Offices</b></li>
              <p>The offices are those of Chair, Chair-elect, Program chair, Treasurer, and Secretary. The Chair-elect, Program chair, Treasurer, and Secretary are elected by the membership for staggered two year terms. The Chair-elect succeeds the office of Chair for a term of two years. The elected officers constitute the ISBA/Biostat & Pharma Executive Committee, which shall follow the general policies established by the ISBA Board and shall conduct the affairs of the section between meetings of the Board. The ISBA/Biostat & Pharma Executive Committee shall report to the Board at each Board meeting. The report can be in writing. The Section Chair convenes and chairs meetings of the ISBA/Biostat & Pharma Executive Committee and the Section membership. The duties of the Secretary, Treasurer and the Program Chair are as described in item 4.B through D of the ISBA constitution, but restricted to the Section. The Secretary will also act as the webmaster for the Section. The Program Chair additionally works, with the other members of the Executive Committee, to organize conferences, workshops, and short courses. The right to enter into legal contracts for ISBA or ISBA/Biostat & Pharma is vested solely in the ISBA Executive Committee.</p>
              <li><b>Additional Provisions for Elections of Section Officers</b></li>
              <p>Each year a five-member Nominating Committee will nominate candidates for Section offices. Three members of the Committee will be elected by the Executive Committee based on suggestions from the Section membership. To facilitate this process, for every election year, the Section Chair will request suggestions from the Section members. The Executive Committee will elect three members from the suggested names and appoint one of the three members as Chair of the Nominating Committee. The remaining two positions in the committee will be filled by the two current officers who will be replaced in the upcoming election. The Nominating Committee selects and gets consent to stand for election from, at least two candidates for each office. The term for all officers starts on January 1 following the election.</p>
              <li><b>Section Memberships</b></li>
              <p>Any ISBA member who pays the Section membership fee is a member of the section. The Section membership fee is set by Biostat & Pharma Executive Committee and approved by the ISBA Board by resolution.</p>
              <li><b>Annual Reports</b></li>
              <p>The Secretary will be responsible for submitting all Section reports, including annual reports of Section activities to the ISBA Board.</p>
          </ol>
        </div>

        <br>
        <br>

      </div>

    </section>
